newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares continue bull-run on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares continue bull-run on Friday.

text.p: Prospects of lower interest rates and an increase in the level of foreign shareholding on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange continued fuelling a bull-run on Friday with brokers seeing no slowing next week.
The key industrial index soared 257.80 points -- or 4.1 percent -- to close at a record 6,499.10. This was an unprecedented 690.90 point surge on the week.

"The market is getting firmer and firmer. It doesn't look like it's going to let up at all and it's quite clear that a lot of investment funds will be looking at the stock market rather than the money market where rates are falling," one broker said.
"At this rate the (industrial) index should be hitting 7,000 soon," he added.

The ZSE's bull-run gained further impetus this week when the central Reserve Bank on Wednesday raised to 40 percent from 35 percent the amount of equity foreigners are allowed to buy in a Zimbabwean company.

Brokers and market officials said they expected fresh foreign investment flows following the announcement, noting that a couple of counters, notably conglomerate TA Holdings, had reached the 35 percent ceiling.
"I think the market's upward trend is sustainable because there is a lot of good news," another broker said.

Leading Friday's winners, cigarette manufacturer Rothmans jumped 500 cents to 3,000, blue-chip conglomerate Delta surged 250 cents to 3,150, bankers Barclays rose 150 cents to 2,200 and clothing retailer Edgars gained 100 cents to 2,800.

Sugar refinery ZSR and finance group Finhold climbed 50 cents each to 1,000 and 750 respectively while multi-industrial group Mash at 130, sugar producer Hippo at 760 and pharmaceutical group Caps at 210 all gained 10 cents.
Textiler David Whitehead was the day's only loser, easing two cents to 55 cents.
Minings held steady and the mining index closed unmoved at 1,320.77 -- a jump of 42.74 points on the week.
